items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: And I dictated these to Lee Smith, who naturally hearing it verbally misspelled half of the names of musicians, which we still do.

ctx.x: The early ones are not available?

No, at best. And also, I have a note here I noticed right here in front of me. I think the 1919 and 1920 files were missing, even in 1938 when I went there, in December of 1938. But I have some of these notes, which I'll go over, and might be able to enlarge a little bit on them. These are rather sketchy. Put on ahead. I mean, I'll send them down to Missouri. I see. Because it's a job that's going to take hours and days to go over that. And I'll copy it out, and it'll have to be by longhand, and I'll send a…
There's also a lot of material there that's invaluable. And we ought to be sure and get recorded some way.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: And Steve Smith's wife would type it out.

ctx.x: So you researched the King Oliver chapter?

Partly. I wouldn't say that. Just the people in Chicago. Right. Because after all, Oliver did most of his important recording and you might say later playing in Chicago. So a lot of people there knew him and several members of the band were still living like, of course, Lil and Louie. And Bill Johnson, Dodds, both the Dodds brothers. So Ramsey couldn't get away from his job at Harcourt. So I did that work for him. All that we could. Unfortunately, no tape machines then. Just had to do it longhand. And I'd take…
Was Steve Smith's wife really interested and involved in things?
